channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Consolidates near 158.55/38.2% Fibo. before the next leg up
item.description: The USD/JPY pair extends the range play through the Asian session on Friday, stalling this week's solid recovery from its lowest level since May, touched in the aftermath of a joint US-Japan intervention.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens as increased risk aversion boosts safe-haven US Dollar
item.description: USD/CHF extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 0.8130 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) gains strength, driven by renewed safe-haven demand amid escalating Middle East tensions.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Friday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Gold trades above $4,250; upside seems capped as Fed hike bets support USD ahead of US NFP
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts some dip-buyers during the Asian session on Friday, stalling the previous day's retracement slide from levels just above the $4,300 mark, or the highest since June 18. The commodity currently trades just above $4,250 and seems poised to register its best week since January.

item.title: Saudi Arabia warns to step up attacks on Houthis – The Guardian
item.description: According to a report from The Guardian, Saudi Arabia aims to extend its military operations against Iran-aligned Houthis for attacking the Najran province, which is located in its southern region, and Yemeni government troops.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds losses against Japanese Yen following China’s Trade Balance data
item.description: AUD/JPY halts its three-day winning streak, trading around 111.30 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency cross depreciates as the Australian Dollar (AUD) loses ground, driven by a surge in global safe-haven demand.

item.title: British Pound remains weaker as UK-US yields narrow, US Dollar strengthens
item.description: GBP/USD extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.3450 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair depreciates as the British Pound (GBP) softens even as United Kingdom (UK) political risk fades.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises to near $62.20 in countdown to US NFP data
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades 1% higher to near $62.20 during the Asian trading session on Friday. The white metal rises ahead of the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for July, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar hangs near weekly low after China's trade data as USD bulls await NFP
item.description: The NZD/USD pair sticks to a negative bias for the second consecutive day and trades near the lower end of its weekly range, around the 0.5865 region, during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: China’s July Trade Balance: Surplus widens more than expected to $112.5 billion
item.description: China's Trade Balance for July, in US Dollar (USD) terms, arrives at $112.5 billion, higher than the $107.0 billion expected, but lower than the prior release of 125.62 billion.

item.title: United States Dollar Index holds steady near 100.00 as bulls await US NFP amid Iran risks
item.description: The United States Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, consolidates during the Asian session on Friday as traders keenly await the release of the closely-watched US monthly jobs data.

item.title: Australian Dollar bulls remains on the sidelines as Iran risks support USD ahead of US NFP
item.description: The AUD/USD pair steadies around the 0.7030-0.7025 region during the Asian session on Friday as traders opt to wait for the release of the closely watched US monthly employment details before placing fresh directional bets.

item.title: Euro weakens against US Dollar amid Middle East tensions
item.description: EUR/USD extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.1520 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair faces downward pressure as the US Dollar (USD) gains strength, propelled by renewed safe-haven demand among global investors.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens as safe-haven demand supports US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 1.4020 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair continues to gain ground as the US Dollar (USD) benefits from revived safe-haven demand.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7904 vs. 6.7895 previous
item.description: On Friday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7904 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7895 and 6.7548 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Japanese Yen hangs near weekly low after weak spending data as USD bulls await US NFP
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is seen consolidating this week's solid recovery gains from the 155.25-155.20 region, the lowest since May, touched in the aftermath of a joint US-Japan intervention, and holds steady near the weekly top.

item.title: WTI holds firm near $77.50 as escalating Middle East tensions threaten oil supply routes
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price remains steady after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $77.50 per barrel during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Bullish tone with upside tests against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH is trading with a soft underlying tone, with scope for the Dollar to test support levels near 6.7420 in the short term, while a sustained break lower is seen as unlikely.

item.title: South Korean Won: Stable Fed and AI demand support KRW against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song highlight a sharp 8% drop in USD/KRW earlier in the second quarter, driven by temporary flows such as Hynix ADR repatriation and National Pension Service hedging adjustments, alongside a hawkish Bank of Korea (BoK) hike.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risk capped against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD stayed broadly flat on Wednesday, trading between 1.2804 and 1.2825 and closing at 1.2810.

item.title: Philippine Peso: Inflation and politics weigh on PHP against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song warn that upside inflation risks are re-emerging for the Philippine Peso (PHP), driven by recovering Oil prices and expectations of a strong El Niño that could spark a food-price shock. Rising global rice and fertiliser prices add to pressures.

item.title: Fed’s Musalem backs rate hikes, says inflation remains too high
item.description: The St. Louis Fed President, Alberto Musalem, stressed that “inflation is too high” and that it’s “critical” that monetary policy focuses on bringing down inflation.

item.title: Mexican Peso strengthens as Banxico hold extends 10-day rally
item.description: The Mexican peso extends its rally to 10 straight days, gaining over 0.12% on Thursday after the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) left interest rates unchanged. At the time of writing, the USD/MXN exotic pair trades at 17.21, after reaching a daily high of 17.26.

item.title: Indonesia: Headline GDP strength, mixed momentum – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economist Kunal Kundu notes Indonesia’s 2Q26 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew 5.3% year-on-year, beating the bank’s 5.1% forecast, but warns the composition is less reassuring.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar drops amid a firmer US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades lower near the 0.5900 level at the time of writing, with no New Zealand catalyst behind the move. The US Dollar Index (DXY) is up 0.26% near the 100.00 level, and the Kiwi is simply on the wrong side of it.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms ahead of Nonfarm Payrolls as Hormuz risk returns
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) posted gains against every major currency on Thursday, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) up 0.26% near the 100.00 level as Oil rallied 3% on the reported Strait of Hormuz vessel ban, while Gold and Silver declined.

item.title: Thailand: Supply-led pressures and prolonged hold for BoT – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research, led by economists Enrico Tanuwidjaja and Sathit Talaengsatya, analyzes Thailand’s July CPI undershoot driven by lower fuel prices while core inflation edges higher.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Policy uncertainty weighs on IDR against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song flag renewed policy uncertainty for the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) after the surprise resignation of Bank Indonesia’s (BI) governor, just as sentiment toward Indonesian assets was improving.

item.title: South Korean Won: Flow reversal case builds – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategist Kiyong Seong turns tactically constructive on USD/KRW, arguing that recent Won strength has been driven by late-stage flow factors rather than fundamentals.

item.title: British Pound: Sentiment offsets softer spreads – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s team notes the Pound is fractionally weaker versus the Dollar, with fundamentals less supportive as yield spreads soften. However, sentiment is improving as markets fade earlier political concerns following PM Burnham’s arrival and stronger-than-expected construction PMI.
